findings.title: Close the final signal handoff window
findings.body:
Close the final signal handoff window**

When no signal has yet been latched, keeping these handlers installed through process exit creates a lost-signal window: `end_by_latched_signal()` snapshots `STOP["signal"]`, and a SIGTERM delivered after that read but before the `return` is merely latched, after which `sys.exit(status)` exits normally. I reproduced this by delivering SIGTERM with a line trace at the `if number is None` line; the alert probe returned 0 with `STOP["signal"] == SIGTERM`, and the mirrored push probe has the same path. Block handled signals across this final check/handoff or restore their previous dispositions when the snapshot is empty.
before_the_repairs: R1 alert: SIGTERM after the snapshot line -> child exit 0 (-15 = ended BY SIGTERM; 0 = the signal was lost) | returned; latch = 15
R1 push: SIGTERM after the snapshot line -> child exit 0 (-15 = ended BY SIGTERM; 0 = the signal was lost) | returned; latch = 15
after_the_repairs: R1 alert: SIGTERM after the snapshot line -> child exit -15 (-15 = ended BY SIGTERM; 0 = the signal was lost) |
R1 push: SIGTERM after the snapshot line -> child exit -15 (-15 = ended BY SIGTERM; 0 = the signal was lost) |
findings.repair: `end_by_latched_signal` is the last safe point and the end of the latch's life: with the handled signals blocked it reads the latch; a latched signal ends the process BY it; with none latched every handler that is still the latch goes back to the default action and the old mask returns, so a signal that is pending or lands later ends the process by its default action (a signal the parent ignored stays ignored). The handoff is run once, in `main`'s `finally` (the probe's `__main__` and the test drivers no longer repeat it), and the sweep covers the handoff and the output after it and requires death BY SIGTERM (it accepted exit status 143 too).
checks_that_fail_without_it: the sweep case (a SIGTERM at each line, now including `end_by_latched_signal` and `emit_report`)
mutant: the snapshot of the latch is read without a block
mutant: the latch is not handed back to the default action when nothing was latched
mutant: an ignored signal is handed to the default action too
the nohup case at the end of the process

findings.title: Avoid flushing before honoring the latched signal
findings.body:
Avoid flushing before honoring the latched signal**

When stdout is a full pipe whose consumer is not reading, this forced flush blocks after cleanup but before `end_by_latched_signal()` runs; because the installed signal handlers only update the latch and return, SIGINT or SIGTERM cannot release the blocked write. I reproduced this with a pipe filled to capacity and a pre-latched SIGTERM: the child remained running until SIGKILL instead of ending by SIGTERM. The derived push probe has the same flush, and the new closed-stdout case does not cover this blocking path. Emit this diagnostic without a potentially blocking flush, or perform the signal handoff before any output operation.
before_the_repairs: R2 alert: stdout a full pipe that nobody reads, a latched SIGTERM -> STILL RUNNING after 6 s (killed by SIGKILL) (-15 = ended BY SIGTERM)
R2 push: stdout a full pipe that nobody reads, a latched SIGTERM -> STILL RUNNING after 6 s (killed by SIGKILL) (-15 = ended BY SIGTERM)
after_the_repairs: R2 alert: stdout a full pipe that nobody reads, a latched SIGTERM -> child exit -15 (-15 = ended BY SIGTERM)
R2 push: stdout a full pipe that nobody reads, a latched SIGTERM -> child exit -15 (-15 = ended BY SIGTERM)
findings.repair: Nothing is written while the latch is installed: `measure` collects its result lines with `say`, `end_by_latched_signal` runs first in the `finally` of `main`, and `emit_report` prints after it, so a stuck stdout cannot hold a probe that has a signal to honor and a signal during the output takes its default action.
checks_that_fail_without_it: the flush case: the real `main`, in children without PYTHONUNBUFFERED, with a closed stdout and a latched signal, with a closed stdout and none (the exit status must stay 0), with a full pipe and a latched signal, with a full pipe and a signal sent once the child is seen blocked in its write, and with a blocked signal (each must die by SIGTERM, or exit 0, and leave no payload directory)
the static case: `measure` and `type_prompt` write nothing to stdout or stderr themselves
mutant: the diagnostic is printed before the handoff
mutant: a failed report leaves its bytes for the final flush
mutant: the measurement writes a result line itself
mutant: a flush comes back before the final kill

findings.title: Remove socket directories recorded during failed controls
findings.body:
Remove socket directories recorded during failed controls**

On hosts with tmux, each `cleanup_control()` injection can leave an empty `<scratch>*` directory behind (and `<scratch>*` in the sync probe): its `failing()` wrapper catches the measurement's `ServerNotStopped` and raises `RuntimeError`, so this function never assigns the local `socket`. The `finally` block learns the measurement socket from `recorded`, and successfully kills its server via `known`, but this condition remains false and only the unrelated `/tmp/tw*` context directory is automatically removed. Remove the parent directories for the recorded owned sockets after stopping them so the selftest actually provides recoverable lifecycle cleanup.
before_the_repairs: R3 bell: selftest exit 0; new <scratch>* socket directories left behind: 2
R3 sync: selftest exit 0; new <scratch>* socket directories left behind: 2
after_the_repairs: R3 bell: selftest exit 0; new <scratch>* socket directories left behind: 0
R3 sync: selftest exit 0; new <scratch>* socket directories left behind: 0
findings.repair: The controls remove the directory of every recorded socket once its server is stopped (`remove_work_directory`: a direct child of /tmp that looks like the probe's own `mkdtemp` result, never the parent of an arbitrary path), compare the directories before and after, and a scope control checks that an unrelated directory and one with the right prefix and another shape stay; a directory is removed only when its server is gone; `tmux_servers()` counts only the processes started with a socket in the probes' own directories.
checks_that_fail_without_it: the cleanup control and the shutdown-failure control (socket directories left behind 0)
mutant: the socket directories of a failing control are not removed
mutant: the removal is not scoped to this probe's own directories
